notes.text: You hold the pawn with b5, ready to push b4 if White challenges it with a4.
Your b-pawn attacks the c5 pawn, undermining White's pawn chain right away.
This is the Alekhine variation, which tends to lead to highly tactical and complicated positions.
Your queen guards b7 and steps out of the way; Stockfish likes this most, and strong players choose it.
Be7 is rock solid and fits your usual approach, even though the engine likes dxc4.
Your bishop develops with the Czech variation and eyes the center, making it harder for White to play e4.
This is a typical systematic setup, but White gets an edge by playing e4 sooner or later.

Protect the c4 pawn with your b-pawn.
